name: vscode-neon-glow
description: Neon glow for syntax highlighting, derived from whatever colour theme is active.

commands.title: Neon Glow: Patch the workbench bundle
Neon Glow: Restore the original bundle

enumDescriptions: Near halo, mid halo and wide bloom, over the edge pass. The look this was designed around.
Drops the wide bloom. Measured at roughly a fifth of the raster time of three passes on a dense C++ file, and the one to reach for there.
The near halo only. Marginally cheaper again than two passes; past the edge pass the glow becomes a thin rim.
neonGlow.glowLayers.markdownDescription: How many shadow passes each token gets. **This is the expensive setting, not `#neonGlow.brightness#`.** Measured over a real scroll on a dense C++ viewport: 12ms of raster with the glow off, 16ms at two passes, 87ms at three. Blur time climbs far faster than radius, and at the widest pass the blurs of neighbouring tokens overlap heavily. A tight 1-2px edge pass always runs and is not counted here: at that radius it costs a rounding error, while dropping it would take the letterform back out of the glow. Applies without a restart.

neonGlow.maxBlur.markdownDescription: Ceiling on any single blur radius, in pixels. The default is the widest the glow ever emits, so it changes nothing until you lower it. Raster time climbs steeply with radius: measured on a dense C++ file, `32` is about a tenth cheaper, `30` a fifth, `28` a third, `26` nearly half, and the bloom narrows to match. A gentler trade than `#neonGlow.glowLayers#`, which drops the outer pass outright.

neonGlow.brightness.markdownDescription: Overall glow strength. `0` turns the glow off while leaving the colours alone; `1` is the default. Applies without a restart.

neonGlow.minChroma.markdownDescription: Colours flatter than this do not glow. Chroma is `max(r,g,b) - min(r,g,b)`, so raising this is what keeps body text and comments out of it.

neonGlow.chromaSpan.markdownDescription: How much chroma above `#neonGlow.minChroma#` it takes to reach full strength. Smaller means the difference between token colours is more abrupt.

neonGlow.floor.markdownDescription: Strength given to a colour that only just passes `#neonGlow.minChroma#`. Raise it to flatten the difference between token colours, lower it to exaggerate it.

neonGlow.minLightness.markdownDescription: Colours darker than this are skipped, however saturated they are. Keeps a dark theme's dim accents from glowing.

neonGlow.cursorTrail.markdownDescription: Milliseconds for the caret to slide to a new position, so the glow on it leaves a short streak behind. `0` keeps the instant jump. Typing restarts the slide on every keystroke, so a long duration reads as the caret lagging the text being entered: `45` keeps up while still streaking on a jump across the file, and much past `100` feels behind. Ignored when the system asks for reduced motion. VS Code has its own `#editor.cursorSmoothCaretAnimation#`, fixed at 80ms; whatever you set here wins over it. Applies without a restart.

neonGlow.saveShake.markdownDescription: How far, in pixels, the workbench jolts when a file is saved. `0` holds it still; `5` is a knock, `12` is theatrical. It runs as a compositor animation on `transform` alone, so the glow is not re-drawn during it. **Turn this off if you use `#files.autoSave#`** - on a delay or a focus change, every one of those saves is a save, and the screen will not stop moving. Ignored when the system asks for reduced motion. Applies without a restart.
